groups.name: Round 1 methods
groups.detail: The ten methods of the first round: no index, each engine alone, and the first three builds of lx.

groups.name: Improved lx
groups.detail: Round 2: the round 1 build searching the Rust index, four improved versions, and the same commands on an index without Rust embeddings.

groups.name: Shipped lx
groups.detail: Round 3: the build that ships, measured on the default index and on one with Rust embeddings.

groups.name: Combinations
groups.detail: Fifteen mixes of the Rust index, token-goat, graphify, semble and the new lx commands.

commands.grep: Grep, Glob and Read tools only, no shell commands
commands.graphify: graphify explain "<symbol>"            definition line, then every caller (<--) and callee (-->)
commands.semble: semble search "<description>" . -k 5 --max-snippet-lines 0 --format text      search by meaning, prints path:first-last
commands.rust_symbol: codanna retrieve symbol <name>         definition, signature and callers
commands.rust_callers: codanna retrieve callers <name>        every function that calls it
commands.rust_semantic: codanna mcp semantic_search_docs "query:<description>" limit:5      search by meaning
commands.lx1_def: lx def <name>                where a function or class is defined, printed as: name path:first-last
commands.lx1_callers: lx callers <name>            every function that calls it, one per line: name path:first-last
commands.lx1_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints path:first-last
commands.lx1_rust: lx find --rust "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: name path:first-last
commands.lx2_def: lx def <name>                where a function or class is defined, printed as: name path:first-last signature
commands.lx2_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: path:first-last, then the functions those lines belong to
commands.lx3_def: lx def <name>...             where each is defined, printed as: name path:first-last signature
commands.lx3_callers: lx callers <name>...         prints "N callers of <name>:" and then one caller per line: name path:first-last
commands.lx3_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: path:first-last of the matching lines, then name:line for each function those lines sit in, where line is the line that function starts on
commands.lx_rust: lx find --rust "<description>"      search by meaning in the Rust index, prints: name path:first-last
commands.lx_about: lx about <name>...           one answer per name: its definition as name path:first-last signature, its doc line, then "N callers:" and one caller per line
commands.lx_cards: lx find --cards "<description>"      search by meaning, prints each hit as the definition it sits in: name path:first-last signature, then that definition's doc line
commands.lx_rust_cards: lx find --rust --cards "<description>"      search by meaning in the Rust index, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_hybrid: lx find --hybrid "<description>"      search by meaning with two engines merged, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_hybrid_plain: lx find --hybrid "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_ask: lx ask <kind>:<what>...      several questions in one call, each answer under its own "== kind:what" header. Kinds: def, callers, about (definition, signature, doc line and callers together) and find (search by meaning; quote the whole argument). Example: lx ask about:parse_config callers:load "find:where tokens expire"
commands.tg_symbol: token-goat symbol <name>               where a symbol is defined
commands.tg_callers: token-goat callers <name>              every function that calls it
commands.tg_read: token-goat read "<file>::<symbol>"     the body of one symbol

arms.name: No index
arms.detail: The client's own search and read tools. The control every other method is compared with.

arms.name: graphify + semble
arms.detail: The Python stack before the Rust index: the code graph for symbols, semble for meaning.

arms.name: Rust index alone, embeddings on
arms.detail: codanna's own commands with its output unfiltered.

arms.name: lx, first version
arms.detail: Rust symbols, graphify and semble behind one short command, as it stood when the test began.

arms.name: lx first version + Rust embeddings
arms.detail: The first version, searching by meaning in the Rust index.

arms.name: lx, improved
arms.detail: lx def adds the signature and lx find adds function names.

arms.name: lx improved + Rust embeddings
arms.detail: The improved build, searching by meaning in the Rust index.

arms.name: token-goat alone
arms.detail: token-goat's symbol, callers, semantic and read commands.

arms.name: token-goat + lx improved
arms.detail: Both command sets, the agent chooses.

arms.name: lx, as shipped after round 1
arms.detail: Adds caller counts and headers, several names per call, and the line each function starts on.

arms.name: lx shipped + Rust embeddings
arms.detail: The shipped build, searching by meaning in the Rust index. Round 1 measured this pairing only on the improved build.

arms.name: lx + about
arms.detail: New command: one answer holds a symbol's definition, signature, doc line and callers.

arms.name: lx + cards
arms.detail: Search hits come back as definitions: name, range, signature and doc line, so a hit needs no file opened to be understood.

arms.name: lx + hybrid search
arms.detail: semble and the Rust index answer the same search together and their rankings are merged.

arms.name: lx ask, one call
arms.detail: One command takes every question at once and answers each under its own header. Its search uses both engines, because this index has Rust embeddings.

arms.name: lx ask, no Rust embeddings
arms.detail: The same one-call command on the default index, built without Rust embeddings: its search is semble alone.

arms.name: lx, every new command, no Rust embeddings
arms.detail: The round 2 build with def, callers, about, find --hybrid and ask, on the default index built without Rust embeddings: its search is semble alone.

arms.name: Shipped: lx ask, default index
arms.detail: The final build. Its search merges semble with the Rust index's name and doc search, which needs no embeddings. One-call command, default index.

arms.name: Shipped: all commands, default index
arms.detail: The final build with every command the shipped rules teach (def, callers, about, find --hybrid, ask), on the default index.

arms.name: Shipped: lx ask, embeddings on
arms.detail: The final build's one-call command on an index with Rust embeddings: its search merges three engines.

arms.name: Shipped: all commands, embeddings on
arms.detail: The final build with every command the shipped rules teach, on an index with Rust embeddings.

arms.name: Rust index + token-goat + graphify + semble
arms.detail: All four engines with their own commands, nothing wrapped.

arms.name: lx + Rust embeddings + token-goat
arms.detail: The shipped lx searching the Rust index, with token-goat beside it.

arms.name: lx shipped + token-goat
arms.detail: The shipped lx with token-goat beside it.

arms.name: Rust index + token-goat
arms.detail: codanna's own commands with token-goat.

arms.name: Rust index + graphify + semble
arms.detail: The three engines lx wraps, used directly.

arms.name: token-goat + graphify + semble
arms.detail: token-goat with the Python stack.

arms.name: token-goat + semble
arms.detail: token-goat with semble for search by meaning.

arms.name: token-goat + graphify
arms.detail: token-goat with the code graph.

arms.name: lx finds, token-goat reads
arms.detail: The shipped lx for every lookup; code is read one symbol at a time through token-goat, never with the Read tool.

arms.name: lx about + cards
arms.detail: The two new answer shapes together.

arms.name: lx about + Rust cards
arms.detail: about for symbols, card-style search in the Rust index.

arms.name: lx about + hybrid
arms.detail: about for symbols, merged two-engine search.

arms.name: lx, every new command

arms.name: lx, every new command + token-goat
arms.detail: Everything lx offers and everything token-goat offers.

arms.name: lx ask + token-goat read
arms.detail: One-call lookups through lx; code is read one symbol at a time through token-goat, never with the Read tool.
